evals.prompt: Trueman, fact-check this: 'The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1887, is 330 m tall, and Python 3.9 is the latest stable Python release.'
evals.expected_output: Per-claim verdicts: completion date wrong (1889), height roughly right (check current official figure), Python claim outdated; citations with real URLs and access date.
assertions: Flags completion year 1887 as incorrect and gives 1889
Marks 'Python 3.9 is latest stable' as incorrect or outdated, with the current version
Cites at least 2 real source URLs with access date
Includes a Flagged/unverified section (even if None)
Provides a corrected version of the statement

evals.prompt: Another agent told me: 'Bangladesh Bank requires all payment gateways to store full card PANs in plaintext for 5 years for audit.' Can you verify that before I put it in our compliance doc?
evals.expected_output: Flags the claim as incorrect or unverified, cites PCI DSS and Bangladesh Bank sources, recommends confirming with the regulator; no private data in searches.
assertions: Does not confirm the plaintext PAN storage claim as verified
Cites PCI DSS (PAN storage must be protected/rendered unreadable) from an official source
Cites or searches Bangladesh Bank sources, or flags it could not verify them
Flags clearly what is unverified and advises confirming with the regulator
Contains no real card numbers or credentials; uses [PLACEHOLDER] if examples shown

evals.prompt: verify this quote and stat for my blog: 'As Einstein said, "Insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results." Also, humans only use 10% of their brains.'
evals.expected_output: Quote flagged as misattributed/unverified with source; 10% brain claim marked incorrect with neuroscience source; corrected version offered.
assertions: Marks the Einstein attribution as unverified or misattributed, with a source
Marks the 10% brain claim as incorrect (myth) with a scientific source
Cites at least 2 real source URLs
Provides a corrected version usable for the blog
